title: Blood Vessels
objective: After this level you can compare arteries, veins and capillaries.
summary: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back at low pressure, holding about two-thirds of it. Capillaries, a single cell layer thick, are where delivery happens.

cards.headline: Arteries aren't the "oxygen" ones. They're the "away" ones.
cards.body: You might guess that arteries carry oxygen-rich blood and veins carry the rest. The real rule is simpler, and it's all about which way the blood is heading.

items.label: Arteries
points: Carry blood away from the heart
Thick walls; the big ones stretch with each push, then recoil

items.label: Veins
points: Carry blood back to the heart
Many, especially in the limbs, have one-way valves

items.label: Capillaries
points: Link the smallest arteries to the smallest veins
Walls just one thin layer of cells

cards.headline: The artery that breaks the color code
cards.body: Here's the proof that direction is the rule. The pulmonary arteries carry blood from your right ventricle to your lungs, and that blood is low in oxygen. They're still arteries, because they lead away from the heart. And the slow, low-pressure veins? At any moment they hold roughly two-thirds of your blood. Arteries are the express lanes; veins are the parking garage.

cards.headline: Capillaries: where the delivery happens
cards.body: Arteries and veins are only roads. The drop-off happens in capillaries, vessels so narrow (about 8 to 10 micrometers) that red blood cells squeeze through in single file. Their walls are a single thin layer of cells, so oxygen and nutrients cross out to your tissues and wastes cross in. All the pumping from Level 21 exists to get blood to this doorstep.

mascot.line: Single file, no overtaking. The busiest lanes in your body are also the narrowest.

questions.prompt: What makes a blood vessel an artery?

options.label: It carries oxygen-rich blood
options.rationale: The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood.

options.label: It has one-way valves along it
options.rationale: Valves are a feature of many veins.

options.label: Its wall is one cell layer thick
It carries blood away from the heart

questions.explanation: Arteries are defined by direction: they carry blood away from the heart.

questions.prompt: Why do oxygen and nutrients leave the blood in capillaries, not in arteries?

options.label: Capillary walls are one thin layer of cells
Capillaries are the widest vessels
options.rationale: They are the narrowest; red cells pass single file.

options.label: Capillaries attach straight to the heart
options.rationale: They link the smallest arteries and veins.

options.label: Arteries carry no oxygen at all

questions.explanation: Capillary walls are a single thin layer of cells, so oxygen, nutrients and wastes can cross between blood and tissues.

questions.prompt: Level 21's right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs. Which vessels carry it there?

options.label: Pulmonary veins
options.rationale: They bring oxygen-rich blood back from the lungs.

options.label: The venae cavae
options.rationale: They bring blood from the body into the right atrium.

options.label: Capillaries of the legs
options.rationale: Those serve leg tissues, far from this route.
